claim: Three people who worked at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Pasadena died or disappeared over two years. Michael David Hicks, 59, a planetary scientist at JPL from 1998 to 2022 who specialized in comets and asteroids, died on July 30, 2023; his family withheld the official cause, and a daughter said he had a chronic medical condition, later identified as heart disease. Frank Maiwald, 61, an engineer on the Surface Water and Ocean Topography mission and on imaging spectroscopy, died in Los Angeles on July 4, 2024; no cause was published and no autopsy was reported. Monica Jacinto Reza, 60, a metallurgist and materials engineer who directed JPL's Materials Processing Group, disappeared on June 22, 2025 while hiking in the Angeles National Forest with companions who lost sight of her on a trail at a cliff's edge; she has not been found. The House Oversight Committee's April 2026 letters name Hicks and Reza.

sources.label: House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform — Comer and Burlison letter to FBI Director Kash Patel, April 20, 2026.
sources.quote: Another JPL alum, Monica Reza, who served as the director of the NASA Lab’s Materials Processing Group, disappeared while hiking in California in June 2025 and remains missing.
